title: Static and dynamic context
caption: Static is set up before the shift, dynamic arrives during it: both land on the same bench.

folder.thing: The folder of the current job
folder.name: Project folder

dynamic-means-loaded-at-run-time.header: Dynamic means loaded at run time
dynamic-means-loaded-at-run-time.description: agents keep lightweight identifiers such as file paths and links and load data into context at run time using tools, instead of loading everything up front [1].

anthropic-effective-context-engineering.title: Anthropic, Effective context engineering for AI agents

before-the-shift.title: Before the shift
before-the-shift.script: Static context is everything you set up before the work starts. Picture the bench before the shift: the instruction sheet, the standing rules and the first work order. For an agent that means memory files, system prompts and your initial prompt.

during-the-shift.title: During the shift
during-the-shift.script: Dynamic context is what arrives during the shift. A worker fetches parts from the storeroom, phones a supplier, opens the folder of the current job. For an agent that means retrieval, web search and your project folder, pulled in on its own while it works.

why-it-matters.title: Why it matters
why-it-matters.script: Why does the difference matter? Because both land on the same bench. The AI cannot tell the sheet you wrote from the box someone dropped off, so the bench has to hold up, whichever way things arrive.
